Nilpotent chains can reach equality in finitely many steps; some nonnilpotent systems remain unresolved at every finite step.
Structural denominator changes can affect output, but alpha=1 or zero active input can leave it unchanged.
Shared-footprint certificate may survive via an alternative support; no statistical independence follows.
A finite bound on charged mutations does not bound repeated uncharged queries, stuttering or waits.
Immutable query replay does not validate concurrent writes from different snapshots; separate commit protocol required.
Individually live supports can form a nogood; filter after product.
Changed factor may be absorbed or irrelevant; full signatures and complete dependencies are required.
Alternative support can preserve the dependent claim.
The converse requires an injective/sufficient representation.
Consensus over true-meaning-containing candidates can suffice for a query.
General dependence admits superadditive realized information; only specified nested/independent cases survive.
Changing only the lower bound cannot certify upper absence.
Intersection and lower<=upper consistency are required; actual completeness is a certificate premise.
Source-idempotence e*e=e is inconsistent with generic scalar g*g=g for g in (0,1).
Independent fair discordant signs or a justified randomization distribution is required; distinct seeds are insufficient.
Cannot-check in one algorithm does not establish nonexistence of a mathematical minimum.

Antichain absorption can remove evidence: {{a}} times {{a},{b}}={{a}}. The evidence footprint is a subset of the operand union, not always equal; shared-footprint membership is only a one-way implication.
